title: My girlfriend and I share locations. Hers says she's in my bedroom closet.
story:
Her dot was in my closet. Not my building. My closet. Ten feet from where I was lying in bed.

My girlfriend was three hours away at her sister's. We started sharing locations after she lost her phone here last spring. We tore my apartment apart. It never turned up.

I texted her. Are you messing with me? She called right back, half asleep, laughing. She was on her sister's couch. She sent a selfie to prove it.

But her dot didn't move. I tapped it. The app said she'd been at my address since April.

Then the dot slid, slowly, from the closet to the foot of my bed.

The room was dark and silent. Nothing was there. So I did the only thing I could think of. I called her old number.

Under my bed, a phone started buzzing against the floorboards. Her old ringtone. The screen glow leaked out across the carpet. Then a long gray hand slid out and turned the phone face down.

I hung up. The buzzing stopped.

Something under the bed whispered, "Who was that?"
premise: location-sharing app shows the girlfriend in the narrator's closet while she is miles away; it's her phone lost last spring, and whatever has been living under his bed since April has it
